activities.caption: file the label sources — where supervision comes from
activities.name: mlpLabelBuckets

config.prompt: Where the labels come from is half the engineering — file each source:

items.label: expensive, slow, biased by whoever paid for it
free, but they encode the past's decisions — the model learns last year's lending policy
clicks as labels — they measure what users did, not what was right

config.why: The supervised paradigm's whole character — its power and its pathologies — flows from one fact: the model can only be as good as the signal in the labels.

activities.anchor: the model scored 95% on its training data, so it is a
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the most important number
activities.name: mlpGapEstimate

config.prompt: A loan model scores 95% on its 8,000 training examples and 71% on the 2,000 held out. Roughly how wide is the train-versus-test gap, in percentage points?
config.why: 95 − 71 = 24 points — the gap between the two numbers is the most important number in applied ML: it says the model learned the training set, not lending.
config.context: Training performance is the easiest score to inflate — a model with enough capacity can memorise its examples without learning anything that transfers.

activities.caption: rebuild the k-means loop, spin to validation
activities.name: mlpKmeansOrder

config.prompt: Clustering's classic algorithm, step by step — put it in order:
items: assign each point to its nearest centroid
move each centroid to its cluster's mean
validate: do the segments predict different behaviour?
config.why: k-means measures distance — it will happily cluster by height when you meant spending, and it always returns k clusters whatever you feed it. Structure earns trust only by usefulness.

activities.anchor: large language models learn without any supervision
activities.caption: true or false — the self-supervised label factory
activities.name: mlpSelfJudge

statements.s: LLMs are self-supervised: supervision manufactured from the data itself.
statements.why: Mask a word and predict it — the answer is in the sentence; the data is its own teacher.

statements.s: LLMs learn without any supervision, so they are unsupervised learning.
statements.why: Supervision is there, just automated — they are supervised learners at heart, overfitting included.

statements.s: Self-supervised models inherit supervised mechanics — loss, generalisation, overfitting.
statements.why: The paradigm is supervised learning with an automated label factory.

statements.s: Held-out evaluation stops mattering once pretraining reaches internet scale.
statements.why: It never stops mattering — the old intuitions about data volume change, but the discipline does not.

activities.caption: pair each problem shape with its paradigm
activities.name: mlpChoiceMatch

config.prompt: Choosing a paradigm by problem shape — pair them:

pairs.left: labelled history — churn, fraud, pricing, diagnosis
pairs.right: supervised — start here, it covers most business ML
unsupervised — budget human time for interpreting what comes out

pairs.left: sequential decisions with feedback and a simulator
massive raw data, few labels, a downstream task

config.why: Real systems are hybrids — a self-supervised backbone with a supervised head, tuned with reinforcement from human preferences: the LLM stack is all four paradigms in one artefact.

activities.anchor: Learn these once and every ML conversation becomes readable
activities.caption: which curve is the test error?
activities.name: mlpUTrace

config.prompt: Two error curves against model complexity: training error falls forever. Which curve is TEST error?
config.why: The U-shape is the train-versus-test gap drawn whole: poor on both sides is underfitting (left), great train with poor test is overfitting (right) — the gap is the field's most important number.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the failure-mode map
activities.name: mlpFailSpot

config.prompt: This failure-mode map contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Supervised fails through its labels: label noise caps accuracy, historical bias replicates history.
Leakage — the 'cancelled' flag that only exists after churn — produces spectacular test scores that evaporate in production.
Unsupervised fails through interpretation: clusters may mirror the data collection process rather than the world.
Reinforcement fails through clustering: k-means will always find k clusters whatever you feed it.
Self-supervised fails through shortcuts — image models predicting from watermark position rather than content.
config.correction: Reinforcement fails through specification — reward hacking: the boat-racing agent looped in circles farming waypoints rather than finishing the race.
config.why: The map's lesson is uniform: every paradigm optimises the signal you gave it, not the intention you had — evaluation discipline is the permanent layer above all four boxes.

activities.caption: drag the divider — model-first versus data-first
activities.name: mlpDataCompare

config.prompt: Two spending strategies at fixed compute — drag between them:

before.label: Model-first
before.text: Upgrade the architecture and hope — while the label noise quietly caps the achievable accuracy.

after.label: Data-centric
after.text: Clean and rebalance 1,000 labels instead — a model cannot learn signal the labels do not contain.

config.why: No free lunch: every algorithm's power comes from assumptions about the world — its inductive bias — so matching bias to structure beats model choice among reasonable candidates.
